clips.title: The story
paras: Meal Appeal is an Orgrimmar errand given by Thatog, an orc tied down by his daily duties who worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. Travelers are asked to pick up a prepared lunch from Borstan's Firepit and track down Migi playing behind Grommash Hold. It offers a grounded look at domestic family life within the Horde's capital.

In the bustling red-rock avenues of Orgrimmar, everyday domestic life continues alongside the drills of grunt warriors and the machinations of the Horde. Thatog, bound to his daily post by duty, finds himself unable to keep a watchful eye over his energetic young son, Migi. Left to his own devices, Migi spends from morning till dusk racing through the city streets with his friends, consistently neglecting his stomach until returning home famished.

Rather than let the boy go hungry yet another afternoon, Thatog arranges for a hot meal at Borstan's Firepit. Because Migi will not bother to stop his games to pick up lunch himself, Thatog asks passing adventurers to act as a personal courier. The errand takes travelers from Borstan's cookfire to the open yard behind Grommash Hold, where Migi and the rest of the neighborhood youths can almost always be found caught up in their childhood games.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: My son, Migi, always takes off to play with his friends all day. I tell him to pick up a lunch at Borstan's, but I know he almost never does, because he comes home starving. These kids think their games are more important than their own bodies!
Please, stop at Borstan's Firepit and tell him you're there to deliver Migi's lunch. You can almost certainly find Migi behind Grommash Hold with the rest of his friends.
Duties keep me here during the day and I can't watch over his every meal.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Of course. Migi's parents and I have an arrangement to give Migi a bagged lunch every day, but I can only ensure the boy gets his food if he actually comes in to pick it up.
Sometimes, he doesn't pick up his meal multiple times a week, and I wonder where he gets the energy to stay out and play.
